text:
opsbot: PAGER — az1b inference pool: sudden spike in 5xx and tail latency. alert_id=INC-2026-az1b-004. kvcache_miss_ratio=0.72, inference_error_rate=0.09, p99_latency_ms=1800. possible cause: mass cold-starts after model rollout. please ack.
ryan: On it — paging in. I'm seeing the kvcache eviction rate jump around 1769998800 across g5 pools. acked @channel :loud_sound:
sara: I'm currently looking at the model rollout timeline — can anyone confirm if a model push happened ~1769998700-1769998800?
miguel: Confirmed — deploy-bot shows a canary push of rdl-v2.3 at 1769998682 to az1b (canary size 15%). Might've caused cache churn.
alex: Logs showing many KV cache misses followed by backend object fetches — backend (s3-ish) egress spiking. snippet: ```
[1769998812] kvcache MISS key=prefix:abc123 -> fetch start
[1769998812] http_get https://model-shard.az1b.internal/weights/part-22 200 18.4s
[1769998820] inference request timeout after 120s
```
ryan: That long shard fetch time is the problem. If nodes are blocking on weight fetch, they saturate network and stall inference threads leading to 5xx.
sara: Impact assessment: hosted API for az1b seeing ~12% error rate on generation requests for customers pinned to az1b. Dedicated tenants that pinned to az1b also see elevated tail latency but lower 5xx since they had warmed caches.
miguel: Quick mitigation options: 1) scale up node egress (add extra instances in az1b), 2) route new traffic to eu-west-2 fallback, 3) enable local disk warmup for the model to avoid remote fetches, 4) reduce concurrency on serving runtime to avoid saturating network.
ryan: Do we have a pre-built runbook for kvcache population storms? I vaguely recall one under eng-runtime.
sara: Runbook: eng-runtime -> kvcache-hotstart.md. Steps: throttle new traffic, force local preload, failover traffic. I'll paste a short version.
sara: ```
# Short-run mitigation
1. set route policy for inference-api to prefer eu-west-2 for new requests: rtr set-policy inference-api prefer=eu-west-2 region=az1b->eu-west-2
2. on az1b, trigger local preload: /opt/redwood/bin/preload-model --model rdl-v2.3 --parallel=4
3. reduce runtime concurrency: svcctl update inference-runtime --max-concurrency=8
4. monitor kvcache_miss_ratio and egress_bytes/s
```
alex: Trying preload now on a couple of nodes. Running: `/opt/redwood/bin/preload-model --model rdl-v2.3 --parallel=4`
deploy-bot: DEPLOY BOT: preload job accepted on nodes [g5-az1b-12,g5-az1b-13] job_id=preload-1769998922
ryan: I'm going to set a temporary routing policy to divert 60% of new traffic out of az1b. Miguel, can you prepare a rollback and monitor for increased latency in the fallback region?
miguel: Preparing rollback plan. Note: routing increases cost and might bump latency p50 by ~40-60ms. Watch for user-visible regressions.
tara: Heads-up — we have two enterprise customers currently pinned to az1b clusters (acct: NovaHealth, acct: DocuFlow). CS is looped in.
sara: Paging CS: @customer-success please notify NovaHealth and DocuFlow that we are mitigating and expect degraded performance for 30-90 minutes while we stabilize.
alex: Preload logs: `preload-1769998922`: 60% of model parts local after 120s, moving to background async. kvcache_miss_ratio dropped to 0.41 on those nodes.
ryan: Routing change in progress: `rtr set-split inference-api az1b=40 eu-west-2=60` -> executed.
opsbot: ACTION: policy update applied at 1769999010 by ryan.
miguel: Observing traffic shift. az1b incoming QPS down ~52%, egress_bytes/s down ~48%. 5xx rate trending down from 9% -> 3% over last 3m.
sara: CS update sent: "We detected increased errors in az1b due to cache population after a recent canary model push. We are diverting traffic and preloading models; you may see brief degraded performance while we stabilize."
alex: Still seeing a subset of pods throw `connection reset by peer` to backend shards — possibly a transient network path. I've kicked a node drain on g5-az1b-07 for investigation: `k8s cordon g5-az1b-07 && kubectl drain g5-az1b-07 --ignore-daemonsets`
ryan: Good call. Also bumping ephemeral capacity: `infractl scale pool az1b-inference +6` -> requested.
deploy-bot: INFRA ACTION: scale request queued id=scale-1769999065 status=accepted region=az1b delta=+6
miguel: Monitoring metrics: p99 latency back to ~600ms, 5xx to 1.2%. Still higher than baseline but improving.
tara: CS confirms both enterprise customers acknowledged the message and want updates every 15 mins.
ryan: We'll keep this thread as primary comms. If things look stable in 20m we can start rolling rollback of the routing split back to 100% az1b.
sara: Postmortem notes to capture: unexpected canary size + cold cache population + backend egress saturation + slow shard fetches. Need to add steps: smaller canary, preload-on-canary, egress throttling alert.
alex: One more datapoint: netstat on g5-az1b-09 shows many TIME_WAIT sockets to backend shard hosts — could be connection churn. Increasing keepalive might help short-term.
ryan: Mitigation summary: 1) split routing to fallback region (done) 2) local preload on nodes (running) 3) scale + drain suspect node (in progress) 4) CS notified.
miguel: I'm seeing error rate converge to ~0.6% after 18m. Will keep monitoring for another 30m.
sara: Planning items after stability: revert routing -> 100% az1b, run model preload plan for entire pool during low-traffic window, add canary gating to preload step.
ryan: Oncall handoff in 45m to @sara. If anyone needs to escalate before then ping me.
opsbot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation in place. current_5xx=0.6% p99=420ms kvcache_miss_ratio=0.18. next_reminder=15m. incident_state=stabilizing.
tara: Thanks team. I'll keep CS looped and schedule a short post-incident briefing with NovaHealth/DocuFlow if this is fully resolved.
miguel: marking this as resolved in pager if metrics hold for 30m.
ryan: closing tasks: keep monitoring, prepare postmortem draft. thanks all. :thumbsup:
